A.name: Scenario A · base case
A.summary: Stock at Reno and the PDC is pooled against every order, a bike can ship the week it is built, and the plan decides builds only.

rows.check: Whole bikes, none negative
Capacity never exceeded; no stock level below zero
No task runs above its run limit
Whole-bike plan within 1 bike of the LP, cumulative, every task
Rounding to whole bikes adds no missed targets
Closure: LP levels = the object's equation run with the LP's decisions
Rollup: pool positions + in transit (+ stock at sites serving no orders) = total net inventory
Shipping projection: nothing negative; on hand − open orders = net inventory
Below target only when the line ran full (or the SKU was at its run limit) every week up to the lead time before

consistency.rule: every scenario passes every plan check
A builds 94,429 bikes and holds every target from 6 Sep 2027 (the frozen base)
E1 takes 3 weeks of 375 off MTB carbon and makes all 1,125 back, nothing else
E2 builds exactly the orders it adds (636 -> 827: +191), all RW-4418, other lines identical
E3 builds the same bikes at other times, other lines identical, no date moves
E4 builds exactly the 300 it adds, all RW-4418, other lines identical
E5 builds RW-9304 only in whole lots of 50, its total rounded up to a whole lot (A's 16,267 -> 16,300)
E5 moves no line's date and leaves the other lines identical
P1 builds the same bikes, holds every target on the same date, clears every order on the same date
P1's ranking moves only MTB carbon; its 'orders past their date first' step also re-mixes road carbon (14 cells, weeks 3-7); base lines identical
P1 brings RW-9304 and RW-4418 to target sooner and RW-6416 on A's date
a change never brings a line's date earlier than its parent's, except by priority
B+E3 builds B's bikes at other times; its MTB carbon date is no earlier than B's
the same 375 a week on MTB carbon in every full week of A, E2, E3, E4, E5 and P1 (weeks 1-52)
R and R+ build A's bikes, every SKU's total as A's
a build time only delays: no line's date in R earlier than A's, none in R+ earlier than R's; orders cleared A < R < R+
R+ takes two weeks from the line to stock on the carbon lines and one on the base lines

R+LD takes 3 weeks of 375 off MTB carbon (2-16 Nov 2026) and makes all 1,125 back; other lines identical; every lost bike is a late order, MTB carbon only, from 16 Nov 2026 (when the first would have landed) to 22 Feb 2027; orders cleared 1 Mar 2027
R+E4 builds exactly the 300 it adds, all RW-4418; other lines identical; MTB carbon (1 week) and orders cleared (2 weeks) move as far as E4 on A

R+C27: every line closed 20 and 27 Dec 2027; the same bikes on every SKU; changes only from 18 Oct 2027 to the closure; never later than R+; built ahead exactly what R+ builds in the closed weeks (1,928)
R+C27: no customer waits longer, any week, any line; every date and the fill as R+

R+C26: every line closed 21 and 28 Dec 2026; the same bikes on every SKU; only MTB carbon customers wait, none before 4 Jan 2027 (two weeks to build: December's deliveries were on the line before the closure), all delivered by 8 Feb 2027
a change never brings a line's date earlier than its parent's, on R+ too
A and every R scenario deliver the most any plan could by every week, on every line (gap 0, every solve certified)

_meta.optimality: every solve certified from its duals and re-solved by interior point (tests/test_optimality.py); every optimal plan is the solver's plan to within what the solver's tolerance buys, under 2 bikes (tests/test_engine.py, no ties)
_meta.deliveries: for A, R, R+, R+LD, R+E4, R+C27, R+C26: at every week and on every line, the fewest units any plan could leave owed, solved and certified, equals the plan's (scenarios.most_delivered; tests/test_r_cases.py)

story.why: R is A with a week to build: a plant cannot ship a bike the week it is built. R+ gives the carbon lines two weeks and the base lines one; it is the build plan. Neither build time is in the data.

_meta.tests: run PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q to confirm the suite that pins these numbers
